article.headline: Natera's Cancer And Prenatal Tests Drive 37.7% Sales Growth
article.deck: The stock bounced off its 50-day line inside a four-week flat base; the buy point is 437.51, 11.2% above Tuesday's close, with earnings due Nov. 5.
body: Natera sells blood and tissue tests. Its best-known product, Signatera, is a personalized blood test that looks for traces of tumor DNA in people already treated for cancer, used to catch recurrence early and to judge whether treatment is working. It also sells Latitude, a blood-based test for colorectal cancer, the Altera tumor-profiling test and the Empower hereditary cancer screen. On the women's-health side it offers Panorama, a prenatal test that needs only a blood draw, and Horizon, a carrier screening test.

The growth is in the top line. Revenue in the June quarter was $752.75 million, up 37.7% from a year earlier, and it has risen every quarter in the table: $592.18 million, $665.50 million, $696.64 million, then $752.75 million. Natera still loses money, but the loss is narrowing: 64 cents a share in the September 2025 quarter, 60 cents in March and 47 cents in June.

The market values Natera at about $56.0 billion. With no profit yet, there is no meaningful earnings multiple; the forward P/E in the payload is negative. Investors are paying for the sales curve. The stock is up 95.4% over 12 months and 69.6% this year, and it ranks 97 of 99 on the desk's list.

Tuesday the stock rose 9.71, or 2.6%, to 388.63, trading 2.51x its 50-day average. Tuesday's low touched the 50-day line, now at 379.22, and the stock closed 2.5% above it. The stock is in a four-week flat base that runs 14.0% deep, from an Oct. 6 high to Monday's low of 376.38. The buy point is 437.51, with a buy range to 459.39; the close is 11.2% below it. The 52-week high is 437.41.

There are earlier entries on the chart. A handle high at 420.25, from Oct. 21, is 7.5% above the close, and the desk lists the 50-day bounce as a live early entry, with the line itself as the stop. The stock is still under its 21-day line at 401.19, by just 0.16 ATRs, and its RS line is 9.1% below its high after an 8.7% slide over the past month.

The next test comes quickly: Natera reports on Nov. 5. Peers have set the tone in the news. TIKR headlines said Tempus AI soared 10% on a third-quarter beat and raised guidance, and CareDx soared 20% on a big Q3 beat and a guidance raise. A Trefis headline Tuesday asked what just happened to Natera stock.
The profile is a leader with fast-rising sales and narrowing losses whose chart is still mid-base, not one ready to break out.
article.watch: The Nov. 5 earnings report and whether Natera holds its 50-day line at 379.22 through it.

article.headline: Pfizer Slips 2.2% On The Day It Reports Third-Quarter Results
article.deck: The drug maker is still in the buy range of a six-week flat base, 2.4% above the 29.31 buy point and under the 30.78 top of the range.
body: Pfizer fell 67 cents, or 2.2%, to 30.00 on the day it reported third-quarter results, and the stock traded 1.65x its 50-day average. The drop left it inside the buy range of a six-week flat base that ran 7.2% deep from its Sept. 3 high to an Oct. 5 low. The buy point is 29.31 and the range runs to 30.78; the close sits 2.4% above the buy point. After hours it was 30.05, up 0.2%.

The stock broke out on Oct. 15, 13 sessions ago, on volume 0.97x its average. It closed 3.4% under its 52-week high of 31.05. The 21-day line is at 29.52 and the 50-day at 28.64, with the close 4.8% above the 50-day and 11.8% above the 200-day. It sits 0.58 ATRs from the 21-day line, an orderly trend, not a stretched one. Pfizer ranks 74 of 99 on the desk's list, and its RS line is 9.5% below its high. The stock is up 20.5% this year.

The fundamentals are the weak part. In the June quarter Pfizer lost 4 cents a share, down 107.8% from a year earlier, on revenue of $15.03 billion, up 2.6%. EPS in the three quarters before that ran 0.62, a loss of 0.29 and 0.47. The company is valued at about $171.0 billion and trades at 10.36 times forward earnings.
Headlines on Tuesday included a Motley Fool transcript of the Q3 2026 earnings call and a Moby call summary. The payload carries none of the report's numbers.
A close back under 29.31 would put the breakout in trouble.
article.watch: Whether Pfizer holds the 29.31 buy point now that the third-quarter report is out.

article.deck: Still in the buy range of a four-week flat base, 1.9% above the 141.72 buy point with room to 148.81.
body: ConocoPhillips fell 2.44, or 1.7%, to 144.40, trading 1.38x its 50-day average. The stock is in the buy range of a four-week flat base that ran 12.8% deep, from a Sept. 15 high to a Sept. 29 low. The buy point is 141.72 and the range runs to 148.81; the close is 1.9% above the buy point. After hours it was 144.44.

The stock broke out on Oct. 14, 14 sessions ago, on volume 0.85x average. Tuesday's close sat on its 21-day line at 143.93, 0.00 ATRs from it, and 5.7% above the 50-day line at 136.59. The close is 6.4% below the 52-week high of 154.28. ConocoPhillips ranks 92 of 99 on the desk's list, its RS line 9.2% below its high. The stock is up 54.3% this year and 62.5% over 12 months.

In the June quarter ConocoPhillips earned 3.23 a share, up 107.1%, on revenue of $19.16 billion, up 36.8%. EPS has risen in each of the last two quarters, from 1.17 to 1.78 to 3.23, and revenue from $13.39 billion to $15.76 billion to $19.16 billion. The next report is due Nov. 5. The company is valued at about $173.5 billion, at 13.22 times forward earnings.
Zacks headlines Tuesday previewed the third-quarter report and listed the company among energy stocks that could top estimates.
The report arrives with the stock in the buy range and sitting on its 21-day line; a close under 141.72 would undo the breakout.
article.watch: The Nov. 5 earnings report and whether ConocoPhillips holds the 141.72 buy point.

article.headline: SailPoint Jumps 5.7% After Hours After Sliding In Regular Session
article.deck: A stalled breakout: even at the after-hours price the stock is well under the 22.38 buy point of a five-week cup.
body: SailPoint rose 1.09, or 5.7%, to 20.08 after hours, as of 5:30 p.m. Eastern. The payload's headlines do not say what moved it. In the regular session the stock fell 20 cents, or 1.0%, to 18.99, trading 0.65x its 50-day average. That close sat 15.1% below the 22.38 buy point of a five-week cup the stock broke out of on Oct. 27; the buy range ran to 23.50. The cup ran 17.8% deep, from a Sept. 24 high to an Oct. 16 low, and formed after a bigger fall from 24.00 on Oct. 6, 2025 to 10.30 on April 10, so the stock is still below that earlier high. Breakout-day volume was 0.65x average.

The regular-session close was 4.7% below the 50-day line at 19.93 and under the 21-day line at 20.37, 0.78 ATRs beneath it. The after-hours price of 20.08 sits above the 50-day line and just under the 21-day. The stock is 16.0% off its 52-week high of 22.62 and 18.2% above the 200-day line. SailPoint ranks 60 of 99 on the desk's list, its RS line 20.8% under its high, and the shares are down 6.1% this year.

SailPoint lost 9 cents a share in the July quarter on revenue of $308.8 million, up 16.8%. It has posted a loss in each of the four quarters in the table. The next report is due Dec. 15. The company is valued at about $10.8 billion, at 47.13 times forward earnings.
On Oct. 23, headlines said SailPoint soared 11% in a cybersecurity rally, and Zacks reported an upgrade to buy.
A regular-session close back above the 50-day line would be the first repair.
article.watch: Whether SailPoint holds the after-hours gain and closes back above its 50-day line at 19.93.

market_note: The S&P 500 rose 0.4% to 7568.92 and the Nasdaq gained 0.8% to 25372.01, while the Dow slipped 0.4% to 51786.72; all three still sit under their 50-day lines, the Nasdaq by 4.4%, the S&P 500 by 1.6% and the Dow by 0.7%. The S&P 500 carries 6 distribution days over the last 25 sessions, the Nasdaq 5 and the Dow 4, and the desk's read stays Market in correction. After the close, Arista Networks jumped 13.3% to 192.50, Duolingo rose 10.9% to 142.00, Super Micro Computer added 9.7%, Primoris gained 8.4% and AMD, which had earnings on the calendar today, rose 7.6% to 520.79, while Toast fell 4.6%. Leadership is thin and tilted to oil and gas: four names broke out this week (Regeneron, Cheniere, United Rentals and SailPoint) and only Regeneron and Cheniere still trade above their buy points, while energy tops the group table with an average RS rank of 68 and supplies five of the eight stocks in a buy range: ConocoPhillips, Cheniere, EOG, Chevron and Exxon Mobil.

chief.verdict: The setups that are working are in energy and healthcare: COP, LNG, EOG, CVX and XOM sit in buy range, and REGN and EXEL have already run 13.3% and 20.9% past their buy points. Tech is where the damage is. TEAM, PLTR, SHOP and SAIL all broke their 50-day lines, the sell-signal list is mostly software and chips (MRVL, NOW, AMD, NET, DDOG, SNOW, ANET), and only 12% of ai infra and 17% of ai chips names are above their 50-day lines. With the Nasdaq 8.5% off its high and 4.4% below its 50-day, the risk is to the downside, and leadership is shifting to defensive and commodity names instead of the growth stocks that lead a new uptrend.
chief.market: The market is in correction, with 6 distribution days on the S&P 500 and 5 on the Nasdaq in the last 25 sessions, so keep exposure light: at most one or two small new positions, the rest in cash until a follow-through day.

picks.why: This is the best chart on the desk. A 30-week cup 25.7% deep cleared 300.99 on 10-29 on 2.47 times average volume, RS rank is 92, and earnings came out the same day, so no report is waiting. The risk is the tape: the RS line is 11.8% below its high and the stock is 9.8% above its 50-day, so a weak market can pull it back into the base.
picks.entry: Buyable from 300.99 up to 316.04, with the close at 311.17 (3.4% above the buy point). Hold only while it stays above 300.99; a close back inside the cup is the signal to get out.

picks.why: RS rank is 97, and the stock held its 50-day line today on 2.51 times average volume, with a 4-week flat base 14.0% deep above it. It reports on 11-05, two sessions away, so starting on the aggressive entry now is a bet on the earnings number, not a read of the chart. The risk is the gap: an earnings miss lands it straight through the 50-day at 379.22.
picks.entry: Wait for earnings. If the reaction holds the 50-day, the live 50-day bounce entry is above today's high (398.13 is 2.4% away). After that, the handle high at 420.25 is the next entry, and 437.51 is the standard buy point (buy max 459.39).

picks.why: This is a sound 4-week flat base 12.8% deep, in buy range at 144.4 (1.9% over 141.72), with RS rank 92 and EPS up 107.1%. But the breakout on 10-14 came on only 0.85 times average volume, it fell 1.7% today on 1.38 times average volume, and earnings are due on 11-05. Don't take a new position into that report.
picks.entry: After the 11-05 report: buy if it holds above 141.72 and stays under the 148.81 buy max. A close below 141.72 cancels the setup.

picks.why: RS rank is 95, and the stock bounced off its 50-day line (50.5) to close at 52.37. It has no earnings until 12-01, which makes it the cleanest tech name left. The weakness is that the 10-12 breakout came on 0.87 times average volume and failed, the 5-week cup is 20.4% deep, and today's bounce came on only 0.55 times average volume. The company is still losing money (EPS -0.22).
picks.entry: Don't buy the bounce. Buy only on a retake of 55.65 on above-average volume, up to 58.43; the stock is 5.9% below that level now.

avoid.why: It is too extended to buy: 13.3% past the 859.44 buy point, above the 902.41 buy max, 21.9% above its 50-day and 4.27 ATRs above its 21-day line, even after a strong 4.18-times-volume breakout.

Its RS rank of 99 sits on a deep cup 72.8% deep whose 10-09 breakout came on only 0.51 times average volume, it has now broken its 50-day line and sits 7.3% under the 206.1 buy point, and it reports on 11-05.
Earnings broke it: it fell 8.7% on 2.81 times average volume, below its 50-day line and 10.3% under the 158.97 buy point.
It sold off after earnings on 2.12 times average volume and broke its 50-day line from a deep cup 48.7% deep; it is now 15.5% below the 207.62 buy point with RS rank down to 54.

chief.watch: Watch whether the after-hours gains in chips (AMD up 7.6% to 520.79, ANET up 13.3% to 192.5) hold into the open and lift the Nasdaq on higher volume, or fade like the other tech bounces have.
